questions.key_step: Differentiate to a linear DE (I.F. x), substitute x+1=t^2, use f(3)=2.
questions.justification: Standard linear DE after differentiating the integral equation; one substitution (L2).

questions.key_step: Subtract the parabola-line region (1/6) from the circle (2pi).
questions.justification: Short two-step area computation (L1).

questions.key_step: [x/pi]+[-x/pi]=-1 makes the integrand odd; or evaluate the floor directly on [-2,0) and [0,2].
questions.justification: Needs the odd-function insight or direct floor evaluation; short once seen (L2).

questions.key_step: Express both sides in a,b,c (Simpson's rule for a quadratic).
questions.justification: Requires recognising Simpson's rule / testing on basis functions (L2).

questions.key_step: Lines meet at (+-2,0),(0,+-2): a square of side 2*sqrt2.
questions.justification: Direct modulus region; essentially a sketch (L1).

questions.key_step: Integrand is half the derivative of tan^4x sin^4 3x after sin6x=2sin3x cos3x.
questions.justification: Disguised product-rule integrand; the recognition step is the whole question (L3).

questions.key_step: Substitute t=ln(y+2); linear in x with I.F. sqrt t; then initial condition.
questions.justification: Non-obvious substitution leading to a linear DE in x, with fractional-power I.F. (L3).

questions.key_step: King's property gives g constant = pi/12; then judge the four statements.
questions.justification: King's property is routine, but verdicts on four statements add a step (L2).

questions.key_step: Substitute t=y+3x, then separate variables.
questions.justification: One substitution to separable form, then a standard integral (L2).

questions.key_step: Split into 2(1-cosx)/sin^3x and 3/(1+cosx); substitute cot x = t (or tan(x/2)).
questions.justification: Two trigonometric splittings and a sqrt(1+t^2) integral; several routine steps (L2).

questions.key_step: [x]=1 on [1,2), x^3=t, sum a geometric series of e^[t].
questions.justification: Floor function, cube substitution and a G.P.; multiple routine steps (L2).

questions.key_step: Multiply by 2cos(x/2): ratio becomes 1+2cosx+2cos2x.
questions.justification: One standard identity and direct integration (L1).

questions.key_step: Combine y dx - x dy into d(y/x), separate.
questions.justification: Needs to see d(y/x), otherwise Bernoulli; two routine routes (L2).

questions.key_step: Separate variables and partial fractions with a repeated factor x^2.
questions.justification: Separable DE with repeated-factor partial fractions and initial condition (L2).

questions.key_step: Split at x=1 for [x]; area under 2 sqrt x minus a triangle.
questions.justification: Standard area with a greatest-integer boundary (L1).

questions.key_step: Substitute 2x-1=t^2 and read off f.
questions.justification: Single substitution and simplification (L1).

questions.key_step: Recognise e^g(g'f+f'), giving f'=sec x tan x+sec^2 x.
questions.justification: Needs the e^g(g'f+f') identity; recognition step (L2).

questions.key_step: x->1/x gives cot^-1; add to get (pi/2) integral of dx/x.
questions.justification: Reciprocal substitution with an inverse-trigonometric identity (L2).

questions.key_step: y=vx then decompose (v^2+3)/(v+1)^3 with powers of (v+1).
questions.justification: Homogeneous DE; the (v+1)-powers decomposition and back-substitution are fiddly (L3).

questions.key_step: d/dx(e^x x^x)=e^x x^x(2+ln x), a disguised exact derivative.
questions.justification: Recognise e^x x^x as exact derivative; one key idea (L2).
